name: runc
summary: A Linux OCI runtime that turns an OCI bundle into a process tree constrained by namespaces, mounts, cgroups, capabilities, and optional security controls.

features.name: OCI bundle execution
features.description: runc is a Linux CLI runtime for OCI containers. A bundle supplies config.json and a root filesystem, and commands such as run create and manage the corresponding container instance.
benefits: Provides a low-level implementation boundary for higher-level container software
Uses a portable, declarative OCI bundle input
costs: The low-level interface leaves orchestration and monitoring to other software
The effective behavior depends on host kernel capabilities and bundle configuration

features.name: Linux isolation assembly
features.description: runc constructs the container environment from Linux primitives including namespaces, a mounted and finalized root filesystem, cgroups, capabilities, and optional seccomp, AppArmor, or SELinux controls.
benefits: Composes host-kernel primitives into a configurable process boundary
Supports resource and privilege reduction without a guest kernel
costs: Isolation strength and compatibility depend on host-kernel features and policy configuration
The composition has many ordering and privilege-sensitive failure modes

features.name: Persistent container state and checkpointing
features.description: runc stores container state under a runtime root, reconstructs a read-only view from state files, and exposes checkpoint and restore operations through CRIU-backed commands.
benefits: Allows lifecycle operations to address containers after the initial command
Provides a path for checkpoint and restore workflows
costs: State files and external kernel/process state must remain coherent
Checkpoint support has additional CRIU and kernel prerequisites

mathematical_views.question: How is an OCI bundle refined into a host process environment with concrete isolation resources?
assumptions: The OCI specification is treated as an input contract rather than a complete security proof
The host kernel implements the requested primitives
Mount, namespace, cgroup, and security setup are abstracted as ordered refinement steps

mathematical_views.question: Which transitions connect creation, execution, stopping, state reconstruction, checkpointing, and restore?
assumptions: A container has an addressable runtime state directory
Transitions have preconditions such as a running state for checkpointing
The model abstracts CRIU internals and host races

costs: Higher-level lifecycle and policy remain external

benefits: Native process model and configurable host-kernel controls
costs: No separate guest-kernel boundary; correctness depends on host primitives
State recovery and checkpoint compatibility are operationally complex
